newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight mkt sees steady inquiry, rates low.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight mkt sees steady inquiry, rates low.

text.p: New business was relatively brisk at the start of the week on the sugar freight market but rates remained on the low side, shipbrokers said on Monday.
"Rates are slightly down," said one shipbroker. "The whole market is down and sugar goes with it."
South Brazil was still being quoted as an origin although the key port of Santos has already passed the peak of its shipping cycle.
Genoc issued a number of new orders for bulk sugar cargoes from the region.
It quoted for 14/15,000 tonnes from Paranagua to Morocco with Mediterranean, Black Sea and Baltic options for end September/early October.
Genoc was also open for 20/22,000 tonnes from Santos to Casablanca with Egypt, Black Sea and Baltic options for the end of September.
Louis Dreyfus quoted for 5/8,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Rio de Janeiro to Aqaba for September 20/30.
Czarnikow Rionda quoted for 6,000 tonnes in bags from north or south Brazil to Lattakia or Tartous for October 1/10.
It was also in the market for 23/26,000 tonnes in bulk from the Philippines to US Gulf/Atlantic with west coast option for September 30/October 10.
Other new business included Mauritius Sugar Syndicate with an order for 17,500/18,000 tonnes in bulk from Port Louis to London for September 30/October 4.
Medmar was open for 14,000 tonnes in bags from Brazil to the Red Sea for September 25/October 5 and
Iranian shippers IRISL was in the market for 14,000 tonnes min/max bagged sugar from Antwerp/Hamburg range to Iran for October 1/30.
